discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 8b3f250c0: each value renders inside its own try/catch, so an unreferenced payload like `{% unknown %}` stays untouched instead of aborting the eval. That matches the behavior before values were pre-rendered, where only strings reachable from the prompt ever reached the engine.

Closed the remaining coverage gap in `6d61bfba6b` and merged current `main` in `9a191e48cab`.

The current catch rethrows when `promptReferencedVars` contains the value, while still ignoring an unreferenced unparseable value. The new non-JSON regression locks the referenced-error side: with the guard mutated back to unconditional suppression, the prompt incorrectly resolves to `{% unknown %}` instead of rejecting; with the fixed guard restored, it rejects with `unknown block tag: unknown`.

Validation after merging `e48ed85e08`: clean `npm ci`, 193 `evaluatorHelpers` tests, `tsc`, the full build, `architecture:check`, both raw-variable built-CLI smoke cases, and changed-file lint/format all pass. No live provider or credential path was used.

Follow-up `08ad16ea3d` covers the equivalent function-prompt boundary found during this review. Reference detection now uses the resolved `basePrompt`, so a function returning `{{v}}` cannot hide a referenced value's render failure behind the raw function source.

The new regression failed before this change by resolving to `{% unknown %}` and passes afterward. Final validation: 194 `evaluatorHelpers` tests, `tsc`, full build, both raw-variable built-CLI smoke cases, `architecture:check`, and changed-file lint/format all pass.

[P2] Keep one unreadable status message from dropping the whole export batch. `span.error.message` is accessed before the new sanitization boundary, so a getter that throws propagates out of `transformToOTLP`; the surrounding endpoint-level catch then skips the POST for every span in that batch. A custom span error object can trigger this while unrelated healthy spans are waiting to export. Read/coerce the message inside a guard and use a safe redacted fallback, then add a JSON/protobuf regression with a healthy sibling span.

discussion_comments.comment_body: The sanitizer is typed for a string and immediately calls `trim()`, but custom spans are SDK/runtime data and `getCustomSpanName()` returns `data.name` without a runtime type guard. A malformed custom span such as `{ spanData: { type: 'custom', name: 123, data: {} } }` makes `transformToOTLP()` throw `TypeError: value.trim is not a function`; `export()` catches at the endpoint boundary, so the entire batch for that collector is discarded. Coerce non-string names to a safe fallback before sanitization (or make the sanitizer fail closed for non-strings) and add a regression test.

I reproduced this on bc86b9c6: with the Pi endpoint returning 401, both `not-pi` tests incorrectly passed in `npm run local -- eval` with the echo provider.
I fixed it in cb04d00d by rejecting non-200 responses and responses without a finite numeric `total_score` before building the result, so errors never reach the inversion ([src/remoteScoring.ts:65](https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo/blob/cb04d00d/src/remoteScoring.ts#L65-L71)).
I reran the same CLI eval: both tests now report “Pi scoring failed with status 401”, while normal scoring stays unchanged (polite: 0.96, pass; insulting: 0.08, fail).
I added coverage for rejected fetches, resolved 401 responses, and 200 responses without a numeric score for both `pi` and `not-pi`; the latter two cases fail without the fix ([test/assertions/piNegation.test.ts:62](https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo/blob/cb04d00d/test/assertions/piNegation.test.ts#L62-L89)).
I also verified that all 2,824 assertion, matcher, and remote-grading tests pass.

**P2 — Reject a tool use that never streams its arguments**

A `contentBlockStart` with a valid `toolUseId`/`name`, followed by `contentBlockStop`, `messageStop: tool_use`, and metadata—but no `contentBlockDelta.toolUse.input`—is currently initialized as `''` and then parsed as `{}` below. The collector therefore returns a seemingly valid tool call, so the normal path caches it and invokes a matching MCP/function callback with empty arguments. That is an incomplete/malformed stream, which this feature is meant to reject before either cache write or tool dispatch. Track whether at least one argument delta was received for each client tool and raise `ConverseStreamValidationError` when it is absent; add a terminal-stream regression fixture.

A custom classifier can return `{ classification: {}, noLabelsDetected: true, error: "upstream timeout" }`. `callGradingProvider` preserves that response, but this branch ignores `error` and emits a normal zero-score verdict; `not-classifier` then inverts it to a pass despite the explicit failed call. Preserve the #10904 guard by treating an empty classification as valid only when `noLabelsDetected === true` **and** no error is present, and add this mixed response as a regression case.

A valid JSON response with choices:[] throws Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'message') outside the error boundary. Normalize absent choices through the shared no-output/error handling before accessing the first message.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Deliberately not auto-marking here, with tests locking in the contract in 2f5dbf8. The scorer is user-authored logic with full visibility (namedScores and componentResults, marker included): if it fails because the metric was unavailable it can return metadata.graderError itself, which mergeScoringMetadata preserves through to the ERROR mapping — covered by the new test. Auto-marking would second-guess the scorer and misclassify the common opposite case: a scorer failing for its own reasons while a metric-only grader happens to be in outage (also covered). The automatic marker stays reserved for grader failures that actually determine the aggregate outcome.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Agree on the direction — quality aggregates should eventually be computed over evaluable observations only — but deferring it out of this PR. Excluding grader-error components from score/weight accumulation changes aggregate scores and threshold outcomes product-wide for every model-graded type (llm-rubric, g-eval, factuality, closed-QA, ...), not just the two paths here, and needs full-suite verification plus a decision on what an all-ungradable test scores. Suggest a dedicated follow-up issue/PR; this PR keeps scores byte-identical and only reclassifies the failure marker.

**[P1] Surface endpoint failures as provider errors**

When either connection emits `error`/`close`, the orchestrator resolves a result with `stopReason: 'error'`, but this formatter (and `formatRemoteResult` above) still returns ordinary `output` without `ProviderResponse.error`. `applyRunEvalResponseOutcome` only short-circuits on `response.error`; otherwise it grades the transcript. I reproduced an error result with one partial turn and got `{ output: 'Assistant: partial answer', metadata: { stopReason: 'error' } }`, so a failed call can pass assertions such as `not-contains`. Preserve the underlying error in `ConversationResult` and return a provider error for the `error` stop reason (without conflating deliberate max-turn/timeout results).
